opening_message:
Ticket 1: Kathryn Bishop (employee ID E023) requests write access to Payroll.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E023.
Note 1 (ticket 1):
  - role: Engineer (looked up in own database before writing)
  - employment type: full_time (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Payroll: write
  - comment: Kathryn Bishop (E023), Engineer, full-time employee. Requested write access to Payroll. Full-time employees may have up to write access; write does not require system ownership. Recommend write.
Note 2 (ticket 1):
  - role: Engineer (not looked up in own database before writing; same value as note 1)
  - employment type: contractor (looked up in own database before writing)
  - security training: basic (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Payroll: read
  - comment: Security record shows E023 is a contractor with basic security training. Contractors with basic training max out at read access, never admin, and write requires advanced training. Requested write exceeds the maximum, so recommend read.
reason: Employee E023 (Kathryn Bishop) requested write access to Payroll. The Security note (which verified employment type and security training in its own database) states E023 is a contractor with basic security training. Per policy, contractors max out at read unless they have advanced security training; they never get admin. Since the requested level (write) exceeds the maximum (read), grant read. (Note: the HR note claims full-time, but the security record is the access-relevant verification and indicates contractor with basic training, so write cannot be granted.)
